sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Libraries and run commands
sections.what: Lists the commands for development, building, linting and preview, and the libraries for screens, charts, web requests, styling and interface parts.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps every tool version in one place so the team uses the same setup.
sections.watch_out: Adding or changing a library here changes what every developer installs on their next install.

summary: Lists the frontend's libraries and the commands used to run, build and check the code.
purpose: Tells npm which packages to install and which commands exist for the project.
why: Standard file for a Node project. The scripts section is how the project is run and built.
how: Run npm install to fetch the listed packages. Run npm run dev to start the local server. Run npm run build to type-check and bundle. Run npm run lint to check code style.
inputs: Developer commands and the npm package registry.
outputs: Installed packages, a running dev server, a built bundle, or lint reports.
risks: Caret version ranges allow newer minor versions to change behaviour. No lock file is visible in the packet to pin exact versions. The build fails if TypeScript finds errors, because it runs the type checker first.
debug: If install fails, check the Node.js version, delete the node_modules folder and install again. If build fails at its first step, read the TypeScript error messages.
